title: Distinct spatiotemporal atrophy patterns in corticobasal syndrome are associated with different underlying pathologies
authors: Scotton WJ; Shand C; Todd E; Bocchetta M; Cash DM; VandeVrede L; Heuer HW; Young AL; Oxtoby NP; Alexander DC; Rowe JB; Morris H; Boxer AL; Rohrer JD; Wijeratne PA
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用机器学习对皮质基底节综合征的MRI萎缩模式进行亚型与分期，属于神经影像疾病分型，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract:
Objective:

To identify imaging subtypes of the cortico-basal syndrome (CBS) based solely on a data-driven assessment of MRI atrophy patterns, and investigate whether these subtypes provide information on the underlying pathology. Methods We applied Subtype and Stage Inference (SuStaIn), a machine learning algorithm that identifies groups of individuals with distinct biomarker progression patterns, to a large cohort of 135 CBS cases (52 had a pathological or biomarker defined diagnosis) and 252 controls. The model was fit using volumetric features extracted from baseline T1-weighted MRI scans and validated using follow-up MRI. We compared the clinical phenotypes of each subtype and investigated whether there were differences in associated pathology between the subtypes. Results SuStaIn identified two subtypes with distinct sequences of atrophy progression; four-repeat-tauopathy confirmed cases were most commonly assigned to the Subcortical subtype (83% of CBS-PSP and 75% of CBS-CBD), while CBS-AD was most commonly assigned to the Fronto-parieto-occipital subtype (81% of CBS-AD). Subtype assignment was stable at follow-up (98% of cases), and individuals consistently progressed to higher stages (100% stayed at the same stage or progressed), supporting the model ability to stage progression. Interpretation By jointly modelling disease stage and subtype, we provide data-driven evidence for at least two distinct and longitudinally stable spatiotemporal subtypes of atrophy in CBS that are associated with different underlying pathologies. In the absence of sensitive and specific biomarkers, accurately subtyping and staging individuals with CBS at baseline has important implications for screening on entry into clinical trials, as well as for tracking disease progression.
abstract_zh:
目的：

仅基于MRI萎缩模式的数据驱动评估，识别皮质基底综合征（CBS）的影像亚型，并探讨这些亚型是否能提供潜在病理信息。方法 我们将亚型与阶段推断（SuStaIn）——一种能够识别具有不同生物标志物进展模式的个体群体的机器学习算法——应用于一个包含135例CBS病例（其中52例具有病理或生物标志物定义的诊断）和252例对照的大型队列。模型使用从基线T1加权MRI扫描中提取的体积特征进行拟合，并通过随访MRI进行验证。我们比较了各亚型的临床表型，并探讨了亚型之间相关病理是否存在差异。结果 SuStaIn识别出两种具有不同萎缩进展序列的亚型；四重复性tau蛋白病确诊病例最常被分配到皮层下亚型（CBS-PSP的83%和CBS-CBD的75%），而CBS-AD最常被分配到额-顶-枕叶亚型（CBS-AD的81%）。亚型分配在随访时保持稳定（98%的病例），且个体持续进展到更高阶段（100%保持在同一阶段或进展），支持了模型对进展分期的能力。解释 通过联合建模疾病阶段和亚型，我们提供了数据驱动的证据，表明CBS中至少存在两种不同且纵向稳定的时空萎缩亚型，这些亚型与不同的潜在病理相关。在缺乏敏感且特异的生物标志物的情况下，在基线时准确对CBS个体进行亚型和分期，对于临床试验入组筛查以及追踪疾病进展具有重要意义。
